description: Eliminate the N+1 query amplification in the Epics list page by adding four stored computed columns to Issues and rewriting EpicQuerier.ListAsync into a single aggregate SQL with in-memory grouping. Performance-only; EpicWithProgressDto shape, HTTP API, and web client are unchanged.

tasks.title: Add stored computed columns (Title, Priority, IsDraft, PrerequisiteNumbersJson) to Issues
tasks.description: Add four STORED computed columns to the Issues table — Title (TEXT), Priority (TEXT), IsDraft (INTEGER/bool), PrerequisiteNumbersJson (TEXT) — each a COALESCE(json_extract(State,'$.camel'), json_extract(State,'$.Pascal')) expression registered on IssueRow + MohistDbContext.OnModelCreating with .HasComputedColumnSql(..., stored: true), mirroring the existing ProjectId/Number/WorkflowRunId precedent. Generate the EF Core migration AddEpicListDerivedColumns (timestamped after 20260625052135_AddIssueIsArchivedComputedColumn) and regenerate MohistDbContextModelSnapshot.cs. PrerequisiteNumbersJson stores the raw JSON array; parsing to int[] is deferred to application memory (done in T-002). Stored columns auto-sync with State, so no write path or backfill is introduced.
acceptanceCriteria: IssueRow declares nullable properties: Title (string?), Priority (string?), IsDraft (bool?), PrerequisiteNumbersJson (string?) — matching the style of the existing ProjectId/Number/Status computed properties.

MohistDbContext.OnModelCreating registers all four columns with .HasComputedColumnSql("COALESCE(json_extract(State,'$.camelKey'), json_extract(State,'$.PascalKey'))", stored: true), consistent with the ProjectId/Number/WorkflowRunId block (MohistDbContext.cs:232-239).

Migration AddEpicListDerivedColumns exists with correct Up/Down adding the four columns, timestamped after 20260625052135_AddIssueIsArchivedComputedColumn; MohistDbContextModelSnapshot.cs is regenerated to reflect the new stored columns.
dotnet build Mohist.sln succeeds with warnings-as-errors clean.

Test (integration, in-memory SQLite applying the migration): after seeding an issue and then updating its State JSON (title, priority, isDraft, prerequisiteNumbers), reading each column reflects the new value with no additional write — verifies scenario 'Derived column tracks State after update'.

Test: an issue whose State omits one of the keys, or uses an unexpected casing, yields null/default for that column and the query does not error — verifies scenario 'Missing or legacy keys yield null safely'.
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Infrastructure/Data/Migrations/<ts>_AddEpicListDerivedColumns.cs (+ .Designer.cs), updated IssueRow.cs, MohistDbContext.cs, MohistDbContextModelSnapshot.cs, plus column-tracking tests in packages/server/tests/Mohist.Server.Tests.
tasks.notes: Use stored: true — NOT virtual. The design (Decision 1) explicitly rejects virtual columns because the list query joins these columns and SQLite virtual-computed-column joins are not indexable; stored columns compute once per write. The existing AddIssueIsArchivedComputedColumn migration is a STRUCTURAL template only (it happens to use virtual columns) — do not copy its stored:false behavior. Generate the migration via `dotnet ef migrations add AddEpicListDerivedColumns` so the tooling emits the correct STORED form; the codebase already ships working stored computed columns (ProjectId/Number/WorkflowRunId) on SQLite, so the pattern is proven.

tasks.title: Rewrite EpicQuerier.ListAsync into a single aggregate SQL with in-memory grouping
tasks.description: Replace the N+1 loop in EpicQuerier.ListAsync (EpicQuerier.cs:21-32) with one raw parameterized SQL query that joins Epics ⋈ EpicIssues ⋈ Issues, selecting only the columns the progress computation needs (epic fields + linked issue Number/Status/Title/Priority/IsDraft/PrerequisiteNumbersJson). Group the result rows in memory by epic (single pass) and build LinkedIssueDto instances directly from the joined columns via a new private BuildLinkedIssuesFromRows(...) helper. Reconstruct CanStart/StartBlocker from IsDraft + the parsed PrerequisiteNumbersJson + the prerequisite issues' stored Status (resolved from the SAME result set), approximate Health as 'active' for in_progress issues (blockedIssues left empty on the list path), and feed the UNCHANGED EpicProgress.Build. Leave GetAsync/GetByNumberAsync/ToDetailAsync/GetLinkedIssuesAsync (the detail path) byte-for-byte untouched. The list path must not call IssueQuerier.ListAsync and must not deserialize WorkflowRuns.State or read Comments/Attachments/agent-config.
acceptanceCriteria: EpicQuerier.ListAsync issues a constant number of SQL statements independent of epic count (no per-epic enrichment query). Verifiable by injecting a fake IssueQuerier whose ListAsync throws and confirming ListAsync still returns correct results — proves 'no N+1' and 'list path does not invoke the full-enrichment path'.
The list path does not load WorkflowRuns.State JSON, Comments, Attachments, or agent configuration (0 large JSON deserializations, 0 enrichment-table reads).
Rows are grouped in memory by epic and the unchanged pure function EpicProgress.Build (EpicProgress.cs:12) is reused to derive progress — EpicProgress.cs is not modified.

For the same epic, deliveredCount, totalIssueCount, and readyToMarkDone equal the detail-path values; Status 'done'/'completed' counts as delivered; 'cancelled' does not count toward delivery or readyToMarkDone.
An empty epic, or an epic whose linked issues are all archived, yields totalIssueCount=0, deliveredCount=0, readyToMarkDone=false.

nextIssue selection matches the detail path's priority + CanStart + no-StartBlocker ordering; a linked issue whose PrerequisiteNumbersJson references an undelivered prerequisite has CanStart=false; a draft linked issue (IsDraft=true) has CanStart=false; cancelled linked issues are excluded from the candidate set.
On the list path a blocked in_progress issue is reported under activeIssues and NOT under blockedIssues; the detail endpoint (EpicDetailDto) continues to distinguish blocked from active precisely.
The Health approximation does not alter exact fields: progress bar, readyToMarkDone, nextIssue, and CanStart equal the full-enrichment computation.
EpicWithProgressDto shape is unchanged; EpicProgress.Build, the detail endpoint, IssueQuerier, and the web client are unchanged.
dotnet build Mohist.sln succeeds and the server test suite (npm test) passes.
tasks.output: Rewritten packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Epic/Services/EpicQuerier.cs (new single-aggregate SQL, row DTO, and private BuildLinkedIssuesFromRows helper), plus EpicQuerier integration tests in packages/server/tests/Mohist.Server.Tests covering progress correctness, nextIssue/CanStart, Health approximation, empty/archived epics, and constant-query-count.
tasks.notes: Mirror the CanStart/StartBlocker reconstruction already proven in EpicGrain.BuildLinkedIssueDtosAsync (EpicGrain.cs:445-481), which builds LinkedIssueDto from raw IssueRow without IssueQuerier. Resolve prerequisite issues from the same joined result set; if a referenced prerequisite number is absent from the set, treat it as not-done (safe default matching the detail path's unknown-prerequisite behavior) and set CanStart=false. Reuse the existing internal static BuildExternalPrerequisites helper (already unit-tested in EpicQuerierExternalPrerequisitesSpecs). CRITICAL: GetLinkedIssuesAsync is shared with the detail path (ToDetailAsync) — do NOT modify it or ToDetailAsync; add the new list code path alongside. Note EpicAutoDoneHandlerSpecs constructs EpicQuerier with a null IssueQuerier — keep that path working. Consider confirming via EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN that the join rides the existing IX_EpicIssues_ProjectId_IssueNumber / IX_Issues_* indexes (design open question). EpicIssueRow carries IssueNumber redundantly which can aid join/mapping.
